questions.explanation: The secondary structure of a protein refers to the shape in which a long peptide chain can exist. There are two different conformations of the peptide linkage present in protein, these are <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="SVG" overflow="overflow"><svg style="vertical-align: -0.025ex;" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1.448ex" height="1.025ex" role="img" focusable="false" viewBox="0 -442 640 453" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><g stroke="currentColor" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="0" transform="scale(1,-1)"><g data-mml-node="math"><g data-mml-node="mi"><use data-c="1D6FC" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-I-1D6FC"></use></g></g></g></svg></mjx-container>-helix and <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="SVG" overflow="overflow"><svg style="vertical-align: -0.439ex;" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1.296ex" height="2.034ex" role="img" focusable="false" viewBox="0 -705 573 899" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><g stroke="currentColor" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="0" transform="scale(1,-1)"><g data-mml-node="math"><g data-mml-node="mi"><use data-c="1D6FD" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-I-1D6FD"></use></g></g></g></svg></mjx-container>-conformation. The <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="SVG" overflow="overflow"><svg style="vertical-align: -0.025ex;" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1.448ex" height="1.025ex" role="img" focusable="false" viewBox="0 -442 640 453" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><g stroke="currentColor" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="0" transform="scale(1,-1)"><g data-mml-node="math"><g data-mml-node="mi"><use data-c="1D6FC" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-I-1D6FC"></use></g></g></g></svg></mjx-container>-helix always has a right handed arrangement. In <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="SVG" overflow="overflow"><svg style="vertical-align: -0.439ex;" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1.296ex" height="2.034ex" role="img" focusable="false" viewBox="0 -705 573 899" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><g stroke="currentColor" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="0" transform="scale(1,-1)"><g data-mml-node="math"><g data-mml-node="mi"><use data-c="1D6FD" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-I-1D6FD"></use></g></g></g></svg></mjx-container>-conformation all peptide chains are streched out to nearly maximum extension and then laid side by side and held together by intermolecular hydrogen bonds. The structure resembles the pleated folds of drapery and therefore is known as <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="SVG" overflow="overflow"><svg style="vertical-align: -0.439ex;" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1.296ex" height="2.034ex" role="img" focusable="false" viewBox="0 -705 573 899" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><g stroke="currentColor" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="0" transform="scale(1,-1)"><g data-mml-node="math"><g data-mml-node="mi"><use data-c="1D6FD" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-I-1D6FD"></use></g></g></g></svg></mjx-container>-pleated sheet.
